name: Nupe raids on the confluence

summary.text: As the jihad reached the Niger–Benue confluence, Etsu Masaba of Nupe took Koton Karfe and Lokoja, both within the Igala sphere, in 1853. Raids grew worse the next year and refugees crossed to the south bank of the Benue. Nupe raiding also reached south into the Okun Yoruba and Etsako country.

moments.title: Koton Karfe and Lokoja taken
moments.text: Igu (Koton Karfe), long a vassal of the Attah, falls to the Nupe.

moments.title: Refugees on the south bank
moments.text: Raids intensify; people flee across the Benue into Igala land.

at.name: South bank of the Benue, opposite Lokoja (approximate)

note: Another account dates the first sack of Igu to 1833; it may have changed hands more than once.
